description: The bar chart, titled "RoBERTa Size," compares the GLUE performance of different fine-tuning methods across two model sizes: "base" (blue bars) and "large" (orange bars), with the y-axis representing GLUE Performance on a scale from 86 to 89. The x-axis lists several fine-tuning methods, including an unnamed method (represented by a gray bar), Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S1-model, S4-model, and S5-model. For the "base" model, the performance is highest for LoRA (approximately 86.7), followed by S5-model (approximately 86.9), S4-model (approximately 86.2), S1-model (approximately 85.6), and Adaptor (approximately 85.8). The "large" model consistently outperforms the "base" model across all methods, with the highest performance achieved by the S5-model (approximately 89.5), followed by LoRA (approximately 89.3), Adaptor (approximately 88.2), BitFit (approximately 87.8), S4-model (approximately 87.5), and S1-model (approximately 85.5). The chart visually demonstrates that the "large" model generally yields better performance than the "base" model for every fine-tuning method tested.
